dataset.telemetry: Elastic Endpoint Security ECS events for macOS
dataset.redistribution: External fetch-on-demand only; corpus telemetry is not committed here.

reviewed_against.policy: A mapping candidate must describe behavior actually present in the file and support macOS. Ambiguous mappings remain needs_review and are excluded from scoring. Multi-technique mappings are retained only when the file contains distinct, explicit behaviors. Mapping candidates remain pending until the user approves this checkpoint and parse eligibility is validated.

mappings.rationale: The captured osascript and pbpaste commands directly read clipboard contents.
The capture reads .bash_history and searches it for network and remote-access strings.
The captured screencapture command writes a screenshot to disk.
The capture copies Chrome and Safari cookie databases from their on-disk locations.
The attack procedure starts Chrome against the victim profile with a remote debugging port for cookie extraction; the launch event establishes the procedure but not the later cookie read by itself.
kcc copy_cred_cache exports the macOS in-memory Kerberos credential cache to a ccache file.
security dump-keychain directly dumps the macOS Keychain.
security find-generic-password -w requests a stored password from the macOS Keychain.
AppleScript presents a deceptive App Store password dialog with hidden input.
The capture reads /private/var/db/SystemKey, credential material used in macOS password-hash recovery; no current macOS sub-technique is narrower than the parent.
The procedure deliberately uses loopback SSH/SCP to read a TCC-protected Safari cookie store, so both the TCC bypass and cookie acquisition are explicit.
defaults reads ShadowHashData from a local macOS account record. T1003.008 is not used because MITRE limits that sub-technique to Linux.
Enabling Safari's Develop menu and JavaScript from Apple Events is risky preparation, but it is not itself JXA execution, TCC manipulation, or a precise current ATT&CK behavior.
Setting a secure web proxy to localhost may support interception, but the configuration event alone does not prove Proxy or Adversary-in-the-Middle behavior.
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine is an exact behavior listed by MITRE for Gatekeeper Bypass.
The command disables automatic installation of critical security updates; current MITRE T1685 explicitly includes preventing tools from updating and disrupting update mechanisms.
launchctl sets DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES to an attacker-controlled dylib; MITRE explicitly identifies that macOS environment variable.
Slack/Electron is abused to inherit an already-approved application's TCC access and spawns osascript in JavaScript mode to execute downloaded JXA.
security add-trusted-cert installs a certificate as a trusted root in the system Keychain.
The telemetry records modification of /etc/pam.d/login, a PAM authentication configuration file.
codesign --remove-signature removes a signature; it does not create or mimic a valid signature as Code Signing or Invalid Code Signature requires.
The capture only proves copies of suspicious ZIP files with Office-style names. It does not contain enough behavior to select a sandbox-evasion, masquerading, or Launch Agent technique safely.
sqlite3 directly inserts an allow record into the user's TCC.db.
kextunload explicitly unloads EndpointSecurity.kext, disabling an endpoint security component.
vmmap inspects one known process's virtual-memory layout; this does not cleanly establish Process Discovery or credential access without additional context.
The procedure searches for Little Snitch, a macOS host firewall and security product.
sw_vers and system_profiler collect operating-system and hardware profile information.
Separate dscl commands enumerate local users and read the domain's Domain Admins group.
The Automator JXA workflow launches a Unix shell that downloads remote content with curl and pipes it to bash.
The EggShell argument is base64-encoded C2 configuration. It is not transmitted data for T1132 and the single encoded configuration value is insufficient to assert T1027 without over-labeling.
The executable /tmp/.xpcproxy uses a hidden dot-file name while imitating the legitimate macOS xpcproxy process name.
A macOS Installer package triggers a preinstall shell script, the exact installer-script behavior covered by MITRE.
osascript runs JavaScript for Automation that downloads and evaluates a remote JavaScript payload.
Python executes a base64-encoded script supplied directly on the command line.
An executable named ReportCrash runs from /Library/Logs rather than the legitimate system location.

The file mixes Bifrost ptt, ticket/cache dumping, askhash, and asktgt actions. T1558.005 supports the macOS ccache behaviors, but current MITRE limits T1550.003 Pass the Ticket to Windows; one file-level label would therefore be incomplete or platform-invalid.
sh launches a bash reverse shell using /dev/tcp. The folder's lateral-movement label does not justify adding a remote-services technique.
systemsetup enables Remote Login, but no SSH session or adversary use of the service is captured.
The captured ssh command opens an SSH connection to another host.

networksetup initiates a configured VPN connection from the host, but T1133 requires adversary use of an external-facing service to access or persist in the victim network. The event does not establish that direction or purpose.
The event modifies .zshenv, a shell startup configuration file used for triggered execution.
The capture modifies Calendar event and plist files, but no current ATT&CK sub-technique precisely covers Calendar-triggered execution and the file events do not prove the trigger payload.
dscl sets IsHidden=1 for the backdoor local user. The capture does not separately prove account creation.
crontab installs the attacker-controlled persistJob schedule.
The sample captures the shell command executed by the cron persistence established for this procedure.
The event modifies com.apple.dock.plist; MITRE explicitly cites Dock plist modification as this technique.
The capture records the command execution triggered by an emond persistence rule.
The sample captures modification of files used to establish an emond rule.
launchd executes /private/tmp/.xpcproxy, whose dot-prefixed filename is explicitly hidden. The capture does not distinguish Launch Agent from Launch Daemon configuration, so neither is added.
AppleScript creates a login item with hidden:true, an exact Login Items persistence action.
pluginkit registers and enables a Finder-related plugin, but current ATT&CK has no precise Finder-plugin persistence sub-technique and Login Items does not cover plugin registration.
A dot-prefixed .espl.plist is created in the user's LaunchAgents directory, establishing both Launch Agent persistence and a hidden file.
A plist is written to /Library/LaunchDaemons with elevated privileges.
defaults writes a LoginHook script path into com.apple.loginwindow.
The procedure captures modification of the root user's com.apple.loginwindow.plist for a login script; unlike the companion process sample, the file event does not expose the LoginHook key itself.
The event creates a script in /etc/periodic/daily, a recurring macOS scheduling mechanism. It is not labeled Cron because no crontab behavior is present.
The sample modifies the user's .ssh/authorized_keys file.
A malicious Vim plugin file is placed so code executes when Vim loads it; current ATT&CK has no narrower Vim startup sub-technique.
The procedure redirects HOME with launchctl, stops tccd, and edits an attacker-controlled TCC.db to grant access.
The sample modifies /etc/sudoers to change sudo authorization.
mount_apfs is used in a captured procedure that bypasses TCC protections through an APFS snapshot mount.
dsenableroot enables and sets credentials for the existing macOS root account. It manipulates an account rather than creating a new one.
chmod u+s directly adds the setuid bit to an executable.
AppleScript runs a shell command with administrator privileges, triggering the macOS elevation prompt.
security_authtrampoline invokes AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges-style prompted elevation to load a Launch Agent.
dseditgroup adds the backdoor user to the local admin group.
